organs::organs-0006::252e5fcd1c2e.note:
I have checked with the ontology, includesWhole has an inverse property isWholeIncludedIn, this seems to suggest that the query is looking for a whole organ, not a part, and the iri in the VALUES has a misleading name.
If that's the case, the generated phrase is correct even though it is too literal, and my previous preferred wording was wrong in that it allowed for a part.
Literal: What is the most recent location and time of the physical organ described by the record Part12_062RhenenGereformeerde?

It is taking the evidence too literally, the organ in the query is not constrained. 
It is an odd query, it's hard to understand why they use a boolean property to find the earliest date for an organ. Maybe the dates are of different form and cannot always be ordered. But there is no guarantee that there is only one FirstProject.

organs::organs-0002::d7142e294be4.preferred_question: What are the given organs called?
organs::organs-0002::d7142e294be4.note:
The previous one should have been approved.
The confusion here is because of the variable naming. A label is usually a humanly readable name, not a descriptive paragraph. Maybe the thinking was that an organ label like “St. Bavokerk, Haarlem” or “Rhenen Gereformeerde Kerk organ” is more than just a name. But description is confusing. It's on the ontologist rather than then on the model I would say.
